references.text: Moses is told to take the staff with him, the same staff mentioned in verse 2, which he will use to perform signs.
Moses takes God's staff with him, referring back to the shepherd's staff he held in his hand in verse 2.
Aaron's staff is thrown down before Pharaoh and turns into a snake, just as Moses' staff did in chapter 4.
Moses uses the staff to part the Red Sea, the same staff that God asked about in his hand.
Moses uses the staff to strike the rock at Horeb to bring forth water; it was originally a shepherd's staff.
Aaron's staff is placed before the ark of the testimony and sprouts, another example of the staff's significance as a sign from God.
Moses again uses the staff to bring water from the rock at Meribah.
